title: Roof-Open Time vs Safe-Weather Window
dataSources: Observing sessions (`astronomy:session`), sky quality (`skyquality:reading`), mount telemetry (`mount:session`), focus metrics (`focus:metric`), observatory roof state (`observatory:roof`), sub-frame results (`astroimage:sub`), and all-sky detections (`allsky:event`).
app: Astronomy telemetry from N.I.N.A., KStars/Ekos, Sky Quality Meters, all-sky cameras, focus routines, roof controllers, and image-rejection logs streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted exports.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=observatory:roof
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(open_minutes) as open_minutes sum(safe_minutes) as safe_minutes by _time
| eval capture_pct=round(100*open_minutes/safe_minutes,1)
description: Measures how much of each safe-weather window the observatory roof actually remained open.
value: This is a clean operational metric for remote observatories because it exposes automation misses even when the weather was fine.
implementation: Collect roof open/close durations together with a safe-weather window signal from your cloud or rain sensor logic.
visualization: Line chart of safe minutes, open minutes, and capture percent by day.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how much of the usable good-weather time your observatory roof actually took advantage of.
